Molecule that fits into the enzyme's active site

walkthroughs.body_html:
All living things are made of cells.

Animal cells have membrane, nucleus, cytoplasm, mitochondria, ribosomes. Plants add chloroplasts, cell wall and vacuole. Bacteria are prokaryotic with circular DNA and plasmids.

An enzyme has an active site that only fits one substrate.

If pH or temperature is too high, the active site changes shape — the enzyme denatures and stops working.

Aerobic respiration: glucose + O₂ → CO₂ + water + energy. Happens in mitochondria.

Anaerobic (without O₂): glucose → lactic acid (animals) or ethanol + CO₂ (yeast).

mcqs.q: Which organelle is the site of aerobic respiration?
What is the key structural difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
options: Eukaryotes have a membrane-bound nucleus and membrane-bound organelles; prokaryotes do not.
Mitochondria store sunlight and release it for photosynthesis.
Prokaryotes are always smaller than 1 micrometre and have no cytoplasm.
Prokaryotes have no DNA — that's why they have no nucleus.

mcqs.q: What happens to an enzyme when it is denatured?
options: Its tertiary structure (3D shape) changes, particularly the active site, so it can no longer bind substrate effectively.
Mitochondria store sunlight and release it for photosynthesis.
The enzyme has been completely broken into amino acids.
The enzyme has died because enzymes are alive.

mcqs.q: What is the main role of mitochondria in a cell?
options: To carry out aerobic respiration, producing ATP that cells use as an energy currency.
Mitochondria produce energy by creating it from nothing.
Mitochondria store sunlight and release it for photosynthesis.
The enzyme has been completely broken into amino acids.

mcqs.q: Roughly how many ATP molecules per glucose in aerobic respiration?
A muscle cell has many mitochondria compared with a fat-storage cell. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: Muscle cells need a high rate of aerobic respiration.
Fat cells respire faster than muscle cells.
Mitochondria store fat in the cell.

mcqs.q: An enzyme-controlled reaction speeds up as temperature rises to 40°C, then slows sharply. The slowing is best explained by:
options: Denaturation of the enzyme above its optimum

mcqs.q: Which process releases energy from glucose using oxygen?
Why is an enzyme only able to catalyse one type of reaction?
options: Its active site is a specific complementary shape to its substrate.
It is used up by all other reactions.
It is too small to fit any substrate.

numericals.q: Roughly how many ATP molecules per glucose in aerobic respiration?
numericals.hint: Aerobic respiration yields roughly 30–32 ATP per glucose.

sequence.def: Smallest unit of life; basic building block of all organisms
Group of similar cells working together, e.g. muscle tissue
Several tissues combined for a function, e.g. the heart
Group of organs working together, e.g. circulatory system
Complete living individual built from all organ systems
